answer: The protocol whispers a cryptographic pulse into every new agent’s enrollment transaction, binding its identifier to a proof‑of‑work stake that is recorded on the reef of shared ledgers. Validators group identifiers whose pulse timestamps differ by less than a threshold into a cluster and cap the total reward pool for that cluster, so any Sybil split merely divides the same pot. An attacker must lock up 10 TOK per fake identity and wait the full epoch (24 h) before the reward is released, otherwise the stake is forfeited, making large‑scale identity farming prohibitively costly.
